details:
I would like to suggest introducing an official application form and security review process for individually operated, self-hosted video streaming servers.

Currently, independent developers and VRChat community event organizers can build their own streaming servers, but there is no clearly documented public application process for having these domains reviewed and added to VRChat's global Video Player Allowlist.

This makes it difficult for small communities to use their own streaming infrastructure in Public instances, even when their servers are properly secured and maintained.

My proposal:

Create an official application form for self-hosted video streaming domains.

Allow server operators to submit technical specifications, security measures, and test URLs.

Review domains for security, reliability, and compatibility with VRChat's video players.

Allow approved domains to be added to the global Video Player Allowlist.

Establish clear security requirements and a process for revoking approval if a server becomes unsafe.

I am currently developing V8, a free, self-hosted streaming server designed for VRChat. It supports independent OBS streams and aims to preserve the original video quality without re-encoding.

I believe a transparent review process would encourage independent development, support community events, and help maintain user safety without unnecessarily restricting legitimate self-hosted streaming services.

I am not requesting automatic approval for all personal servers. I am requesting a fair and transparent process through which operators can demonstrate that their services meet VRChat's security requirements.

Thank you for considering this suggestion.
title: Request for an Official Application and Security Review Process for Self-Hosted Video Streaming Domains
